title: Go SDK: stream wrapper cancellation patterns and coordinated retries
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description:
Problem: The Go SDK streaming surface currently exposes a low-level io.Read/chan-based stream. Users need clear, ergonomic semantics for context cancellation, per-request deadlines, and how retries should behave when partial responses have been emitted.

Goal: Implement a stream wrapper and patterns that: (1) reliably propagate context cancellation and deadlines into the underlying transport and runtime, (2) provide a documented retry coordination strategy that avoids duplicate or interleaved partial events to callers, (3) expose an ergonomically simple API for common cases (single-shot read with timeout, streaming consumer with graceful shutdown), and (4) include examples + tests and CI benchmarks showing latency/regression characteristics.

Scope: Library changes to the Go SDK only (no server changes). Provide backward-compatible adapters for existing streaming helpers. Deliverables include new wrapper types, examples, unit/integration tests, and a design doc detailing semantics.
acceptance_criteria: A1: New StreamWrapper type that accepts context.Context and enforces deadline vs timeout semantics documented in the design doc
A2: Cancellation immediately closes underlying transport and unblocks consumers with a distinct error type (StreamCancelledError) so callers can differentiate cancellation vs network errors

A3: Implement a retry coordinator that prevents duplicate partial message delivery: on retry the wrapper either buffers the partial last-event or marks retry boundary; documented behavior for at-least-once vs exactly-once tradeoffs
A4: Examples in examples/streaming demonstrating: graceful shutdown loop, per-request timeout wrapper, and cooperative cancellation with parent goroutine
A5: Unit tests covering: deadline propagation, context cancellation during in-flight token generation, and retry boundary semantics
A6: Integration test against local dev runtime demonstrating no goroutine leaks under abrupt client cancellations
A7: Benchmarks (CI) showing <5% p50 latency regression vs current master for 1-token streaming at 128 sequence length on CI baseline
tasks: Design doc: detail API surface, error types, retry coordinator state machine
Implement StreamWrapper with context-aware Read/Recv method
Add StreamCancelledError and exported helpers for IsCancelled/IsDeadlineExceeded
Implement simple RetryCoordinator with in-memory last-event handling
Write examples and add to docs site (examples/streaming/graceful_shutdown.go)
Unit and integration tests + CI benchmarks
Code review and address security/edge cases (race conditions, closed-channels)
Merge and cut release branch for sdk-go-0.10
comments: 2025-02-10 Aisha Kapoor: Created ticket after spike. Prototype shows cancellation is not reliably propagated when SDK consumer cancels while token generation is mid-flight.

2025-02-11 Marco Chen: POC StreamWrapper implemented. Key gap: how to avoid double-delivery when server supports resume-from-kv behavior. Proposal: explicit retry boundary markers and an optional dedupe token from runtime.
2025-02-12 Design note (link in links): added doc that formalizes 'retry boundary' and 'partial-event buffering' strategies. Prefer simple buffering for SDK v0.10 to avoid protocol changes.

2025-02-14 Code review (PR #2973): initial review from @OlgaPetrov. Feedback: ensure all goroutines select on ctx.Done() and add race detector CI job. Also recommend an exported error var for easy checks.
2025-02-16 Marco Chen: Addressed review comments, added StreamCancelledError and IsCancelled helper. Added tests for deadline vs timeout behavior. Benchmarks show 2.1% p50 change on CI baseline.

2025-02-18 Aisha Kapoor: Merged feature branch into integration branch for broader staging test. Open follow-ups: support server-side resume tokens if runtime adds them (ENG TBD), and add TypeScript SDK parity docs.
test_plan: 1) Unit tests run locally with -race, cover cancellation and deadline branches. 2) Integration uses local dev runtime (docker compose) to simulate mid-stream cancellation and server disconnects. 3) CI runs benchmarks on the integration branch; compare p50/p95 vs master. 4) Run goroutine-leak detection in CI for 30s storm test.
notes: Trade-offs considered: buffering last partial event simplifies client semantics but increases memory/latency for large events. Alternative: protocol-level resume tokens would give exact-once semantics; scoped out to future work. Need to coordinate with runtime team if we want to rely on resume tokens. Also consider exposing two APIs: StreamWrapper (safe default) and RawStream (existing low-level behavior) to keep backward compatibility.
